nm_poultrygeist_area.blurb: One of four sections of Cockscomb Crag, a basalt cliff in the Diablo Canyon country near Santa Fe. This is a small sport wall with twelve routes, eleven bolted and one trad crack. The grades cluster in the 5.11 range, with a few 5.10s, a single 5.9 and one 5.12 on top. Compared with the neighbouring Chicken Little section, the climbing is more varied: pockets, overhanging bulges, some jugs and a bit of stemming. The walk along the cliff base passes a stretch of crumbly rock before the stone turns solid. A good stop for climbers who already lead 5.10 and want steady, moderate-to-hard bolted pitches.

nm_clandestine_wall.blurb: A steep wall tucked into Chimney Canyon on the west side of the Sandia Mountains above Albuquerque. It has twelve routes, ten of them trad and two bolted, on a face broken by roofs, thin cracks and sections of clean red face climbing. The difficulty is skewed upward: one route in the 5.8 range, a few 5.10s, and then a run of 5.11 to 5.13 lines topped by a 5.14 bolted route. It has a reputation as the Sandias' best crag for hard climbing, so it suits experienced trad leaders more than beginners. Reaching it means a long, committing hike with some route-finding along an unmaintained trail.

nm_gemstone_west.blurb: A slab-and-crack crag in La Cueva Canyon on the west side of the Sandia Mountains, near Albuquerque. All twelve routes are trad, from a pair of easy 5.7s through a cluster of 5.9s and 5.10s up to a couple of 5.11s, and a few run to two pitches. The rock is clean, the angle is friendly, and the variety of moves makes it a draw for first-time trad leaders and groups. Expect a longer-than-it-looks hike from the picnic area: stream crossings, a boulder field, some brush, and a trail that fades on open slabs before you traverse to the base.

nm_wallflower_wall.blurb: A small east-facing cliff just north of the main wall in Spook Canyon, part of the Box climbing areas near Socorro. It holds twelve routes, mostly bolted, with a lone trad line and a top-rope route. Grades are friendly: a few easier pitches in the 5.6 to 5.7 range, then a solid block of 5.9s and a handful of 5.10s, so it works well for newer leaders. The wall gets morning sun and afternoon shade, and it is sheltered from most wind. Nearly everything can be top-roped by scrambling up an easy ramp on the right side of the cliff.

nm_waterfall_wall.blurb: The beginner wall of the Box near Socorro, set right beside the main parking area. Twelve routes, almost all of them top-rope, start with one very easy climb and continue through 5.6 and 5.7 pitches to a few 5.10s and 5.11s, with one 5.12 at the top end. The rhyolite is strong but can be sharp, and since it is dark red to black the wall is mostly sunny and gets very hot, so cool days are best. The wall takes its name from a small waterfall on its right side that is dry now and only leaves a black stain. A popular spot for learning and for top-roping with groups.

nm_torreon.blurb: A multi-pitch trad formation in upper La Cueva Canyon on the west side of the Sandia Mountains, reached from the crest side, directly across from The Thumb. It is known for some of the cleanest rock in the range. All twelve routes are trad and most run several pitches, with the grades starting at 5.10 and climbing through a block of 5.11s to a few 5.12s. It is no place for a first alpine-style outing: the walk in includes a short downclimb and a steep fourth-class gully with a loose wrong turn nearby, so go with someone who knows it. The descent is a single rappel.

nm_gateway_rock.blurb: One of the closest cliffs to the parking at Las Conchas in the Jemez Mountains, standing in a meadow near the creek. Eleven routes, ten bolted and one trad, mostly on 5.10 and 5.11 terrain with a few easier warm-ups in the 5.6 to 5.8 range. The routes mostly face east, so the wall takes sun from morning until early afternoon and then falls into shade, which makes it pleasant in warm weather. The walk is only a short trail along the creek. Hikers pass by often, so expect an audience.

nm_a2_white_riot_wall_upper_tier.blurb: A set-back cove on the upper tier of Utopian Vistas, the basalt cliffs of the Taos area. Eleven routes, seven trad and four sport, mostly short, with the right-hand side steeper and facing southeast while the left side starts from a low bench. Grades begin around 5.8, include a 5.9, and then concentrate in 5.10 and 5.11, with one 5.12 at the top. Expect crack and corner lines alongside bolted pitches. The walk follows the upper tier past tumbled boulders, then drops away from the wall to avoid a dead-end bench before a trail leads back up to the cove.
